name: Per Ola Kristensson
areas: Mixed Reality, Text Entry, Human-Robot Interaction, Accessibility, Hand Gestures, Human-AI Interaction, Spatial Interaction Design, Adaptive Interfaces
bio: Professor of Interactive Systems Engineering and Fellow of Trinity College. He co-invented gesture keyboard technology, now built into most phones and tablets, and co-founded ShapeWriter, which Nuance acquired in 2010. Co-director of the Centre for Human-Inspired AI, winner of the ACM UIST Lasting Impact Award, and inducted into the ACM SIGCHI Academy.

name: Florian Fischer
bio: Builds computational methods that study how accessible, ergonomic and efficient intelligent systems are, with a focus on virtual reality. He combines motor control, biomechanics and cognitive science to create AI-based models of users, and co-authored the SUI 2025 best paper on mid-air surface interaction.

name: Jiuming Liu
bio: Studies how to establish world models or world action models for robotics, autonomous driving, and gaming domains. He is interested in accurate 3D scene modeling, representation learning, and dynamic prediction based on diffusion models.

name: Junlong Chen
bio: Completed an MPhil at Cambridge with a dissertation on scene interpretation for visual accessibility in virtual reality. His work includes EnvisionVR and studies of speech, pointing and LLM-assisted manipulation of 3D scenes.

name: Clare Heinbaugh
areas: Mixed Reality, Human-Robot Interaction, Hand Gestures, Human-AI Interaction, Spatial Interaction Design
bio: Studies how people interact with computers through gestures in extended reality, focusing on applications where automated system inference and the user's own control work together.
bioLong: Clare is interested in gesture-based interaction in extended reality. Specifically, she is focused on applications that sit at the intersection of system-based inference and user-directed control. Clare has a Bachelor's degree in computer science from William & Mary in the United States. She completed an MPhil in machine learning at the University of Cambridge with a dissertation focused on teleoperation of multiple robot arms supported by virtual reality, gestures, and gaze tracking. Her PhD is supported by the Marshall Scholarship, and she is a Cambridge International Scholar.

name: Aleesha Hamid
bio: Researcher at the Engineering Design Centre. She wrote a review of forty years of eye typing research and develops interactive rich pictures that surface hidden work in complex systems.

name: Zhuoyue Lyu
bio: Works on spatial interaction design that deepens connections between humans, the physical world, and digital experiences. His research is supported by the Trinity-Henry Barlow and Cambridge Trust scholarships.

name: Ankit Bhattarai
bio: Works on biomechanical user simulation for HCI. Lead author of MyoInteract, a framework for prototyping biomechanical interaction tasks with reinforcement learning.

name: Billy Shi
bio: Studies how people and LLM agents should share the work of software test case development, with papers in ACM TOCHI and IEEE Software.

name: Izabella Sabharwal De Bessenyey
bio: PhD student at the Centre for Human-Inspired AI, working with the group.

name: Shriya Sekhsaria
bio: PhD student at the Centre for Human-Inspired AI, supervised by Per Ola Kristensson. Shriya is interested in how technology like AI affects human capacities like love and creativity. She founded Lumhaa, a memory and relationship app, graduated from Princeton in 2018, and writes novels.

name: Konstantin Strömel
bio: PhD student at the Centre for Human-Inspired AI, working with the group.

name: Oliver Anderson
bio: PhD student at the Centre for Human-Inspired AI, working with the group.

name: John Douglas
bio: PhD student in machine learning, supervised by John Dudley. Research interests include explainable model adaptations for web and extended reality settings.

name: John Dudley
areas: Accessibility, Mixed Reality, Human-Robot Interaction, Text Entry, Adaptive Interfaces, Hand Gestures, Human-AI Interaction
bio: Course Director of the MPhil in Machine Learning and Machine Intelligence. His research focusses on developing user interfaces that enhance human capabilities, productivity, and experience in challenging, information-rich environments.

name: Barry Gao
bio: PhD student supervised by John Dudley. Prior to commencing his PhD, Barry completed his MEng and BA in the Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge. He is interested in Human-Computer Interaction, Mixed Reality and Spatial Intelligence.
